properties.name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
properties.description: The University of Massachusetts Amherst is a public research university offering a wide range of academic programs across disciplines. Within its Department of Earth, Geographic, and Climate Sciences, the one-year master’s concentration in Geographic Information Science and Technology (GIST) provides focuessed training in Geographic Information Science, remote sensing, and spatial modeling. The program prepares students for applied work in diverse settings through a combination of technical coursework and practical experience.
properties.experience: I completed my graduate degree in Geographic Information Science and Technology (GIST) at UMass Amherst, where I gained hands-on experience in spatial analysis, remote sensing, and GIS application design. The program emphasized both technical proficiency and real-world impact, preparing me to contribute to transportation and environmental data projects with confidence and precision. My coursework and practicum experiences laid the foundation for my work with organizations like MassDOT and the Charles River Conservancy.

gallery.caption: An exerpt from a brochure I made for my Environmental Geography & Sustainability course, where I illustrated the geographical changes of the Charles River over the historical development of Boston. Notice how the Charles River basin has become constricted, and how the shoreline has been expanded and straightened. Creation of this map employed techniques such as georeferencing, creation of features, utilizing open data, and more.

During my time taking the course Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, I learned how to process and interpret raster data. Pictured is the result of some lab work, where I practiced classifying a satellite image based on land use. This course taught me the foundations of using GIS imagery as well as the mechanisms of remote sensing.

During my time taking the course Spatial Databases & Data Interoperability, I learned how to code with HTML and JavaScript, retrieve data with SQL, and utilize FME - a model builder meant to manage data in an automized way. Pictured is my actual workflow for the Vegetation Monitoring Dashboard I created, which you can learn more from another waypoint on the map.

properties.name: Charles River Conservancy
properties.description: The Charles River Conservancy is a nonprofit organization dedicated to enhancing and maintaining the parks and natural habitats along the Charles River in Greater Boston. Through ecological restoration, volunteer stewardship, and public engagement, CRC works to preserve biodiversity and promote equitable access to green spaces. Its initiatives include invasive species management, environmental monitoring, and creative programming in urban wilds like Hell’s Half Acre.
properties.experience: As a volunteer with CRC, I contributed over 100 hours to invasive species monitoring and urban park restoration along the Charles and in Hell’s Half Acre, an urban wild in Cambridge, MA. In addition to my fieldwork as a CREW Steward and Vegetation Monitor, I developed an ArcGIS dashboard as part of a final project for one of my graduate courses. The tool visualizes plant coverage data collected by volunteers and is now featured on CRC’s website. The dashboard was designed to support CRC’s restoration efforts and make ecological data more accessible to both the organization and the public.

gallery.caption: I am passionate about my volunteer work with the Charles River Conservancy, where I act as a CREW Steward and Vegetation Monitor. Through the CREW program, I take care of an assigned section of the Charles by collecting litter and removing/reporting invasive species. Through the Vegetation Monitoring program, I record the growth of plants in a local urban wild in response to restoration efforts. To expand on my volunteer work with the CRC and in an effort to introduce a GIS perspective to the organization, I created this Vegetation Monitoring Dashboard to make our findings accessible to the public and interpretable by the CRC. You can select by species & habitat type to visualize plant distributions based on their ground coverage throughout the year.

properties.name: 18b TIP
properties.description: 18b TIP is a community-based initiative in Suffolk County, NY that supports formerly incarcerated individuals through social work, resource navigation, and reintegration services. The program focuses on personalized outreach and geographic accessibility, helping clients connect with housing, employment, health care, and other essential services as they transition back into society.
properties.experience: At 18b TIP, I led the development of an interactive GIS dashboard using ArcGIS Experience Builder to centralize community resources for formerly incarcerated individuals in Suffolk County. The dashboard is actively used by the organization’s team of social workers, legal professionals, and their interns to recommend geographically relevant services to their clients. Working iteratively with my supervisor, I structured the data, designed the interface, and introduced layered filtering tools to support intuitive navigation and personalized outreach. The dashboard continues to evolve as the team’s needs grow, offering a flexible platform for ongoing updates and community engagement.

gallery.caption: Here is the main page of the Suffolk County 18b TIP resource dashboard. The user enters the client's address and specifies any relevant catgeory filters. On the left is a list of all nearby resources along with location/web addresses, resource descriptions, and contact info. The map at the bottom right visualizes the filtered resources within the search area.

The Settings tab allows the user to customize the output of the resource list. In this case, resources will not appear separated by category, will not order starred resources at the top of this list, and will shorten each record by hiding resource descriptions. This feature allows for a flexible output that can easily be sent to clients with minimal editing required.

This is the Hotlines & Helplines page. While not GIS, it is still data-based and makes use of extensive filtering. In this case, all resources reflect the selected filters of Hotlines or Helplines specializing in Mental Health or LGBTQ Concerns that support Spanish-speaking individuals.

properties.name: MassDOT
properties.description: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) oversees transportation infrastructure across the Commonwealth, including highways, public transit, aeronautics, and rail. Through its divisions and open data initiatives, MassDOT advances statewide goals in planning, safety, and accessibility. The agency also maintains a robust GIS program that provides spatial datasets for roadways, environmental assets, multimodal networks, and more.
properties.experience: As part of my graduate practicum, I worked remotely with MassDOT to digitize speed regulation records into a centralized GIS layer. My focus was on Southeast Massachusetts, contributing to a broader initiative to improve data consistency and accessibility across the state. While I didn’t visit the region in person, the project gave me practical experience with structured workflows and demonstrated how foundational GIS work supports transportation planning and analysis across the agency.

gallery.caption: During my graduate practicum at UMass Amherst, I worked with MassDOT to digitize speed regulation records from paper format into a GIS layer. The image shows a paper speed regulation on the left and the GIS system on the right, which we used to modernize this data. Though the task was detailed and manual, it taught me of the essential role GIS plays in supporting our public infrastructure. Now that these records have been digitized, MassDOT is able to spatially analyze speed regulations across Massachusetts and can leverage this information to inform future projects.

properties.name: Warwick Water Division
properties.description: The Warwick Water Division is responsible for providing safe, reliable, and sustainable water services to Warwick residents and businesses. The division manages water supply and distribution, infrastructure maintenance and upgrades, leak detection, regulatory compliance, and emergency response to ensure continuous access to clean drinking water and maintain system reliability.
properties.experience: As GIS Coordinator, I remediated a system with significant data inconsistencies and geometric errors by restructuring the schema, standardizing attribute values, and correcting pipe geometry. A key accomplishment was linking historic as-built record scans to infrastructure features using relational tables, making records instantly accessible to staff when they click on an asset. I also trained field staff on Field Maps and GNSS protocols, developed an ArcGIS Online dashboard for real-time field tracking and impact metrics, and advocated for expanded ArcGIS Pro licensing to strengthen data integrity and drive cross-departmental adoption.

gallery.caption: The Warwick Water GIS Viewer, built in ArcGIS Experience Builder, serves as the primary interface for accessing and exploring potable water infrastructure data. The application displays hydrants, valves, connecting pipes, and more as an integrated network, complete with search functionality and filtering widgets enabling staff to quickly locate and inspect assets. Clicking on various features pulls up all related records to further contextualize the asset layout. This integrated approach ensures staff rely on authoritative GIS data and enables efficient, location-based workflows for water system management.

The Field Mapping Dashboard provides real-time visibility into GNSS mapping efforts, including progress logs, temporal trends, and impact statistics. This dashboard enhances team accountability and enables management to monitor field collection activity across asset types. Providing this transparency reinforces the adoption of GIS workflows and the use of GNSS receivers across the Water Division.
